Which of these four appeared earliest?
Pascal (programming language) (published 1972) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these is a physicist?
John Tyndall is a physicist. John Tyndall (2 August 1820 – 4 December 1893) was an Irish physicist.
What is the atomic number of Niobium?
Niobium is a chemical element; it has symbol Nb (formerly columbium, Cb) and atomic number 41.
What is the atomic number of Phosphorus?
Phosphorus is a chemical element; it has symbol P and atomic number 15.
In what year was Jordan Peterson born?
Jordan Peterson: Jordan Bernt Peterson (born 12 June 1962) is a Canadian psychologist, author, and media commentator.
In what year was Proxima Centauri discovered?
Proxima Centauri is the nearest star to Earth after the Sun, located 4.25 light-years (1.3 parsecs) away in the southern constellation of Centaurus.
In what year was Bromine discovered?
Bromine is a chemical element; it has symbol Br and atomic number 35.

Gabapentin: Pfizer. Gabapentin is a
central nervous system (CNS) depressant and derivative of the inhibitory neurotransmitter, GABA.
In which country is IAI Kfir?
Who is credited with discovering Penicillin?
Penicillin: Alexander Fleming. Penicillin was discovered in 1928 by the Scottish physician Alexander Fleming as a crude extract of P. rubens.
2C-B: Alexander Shulgin. 2C-B, also known as 4-bromo-2,5-dimethoxyphenethylamine or by names such as Nexus or Erox, is a psychedelic drug of the phenethylamine and 2C families.
Who is credited with discovering Chromium?
Chromium: Louis Nicolas Vauquelin. Chromium is a chemical element; it has symbol Cr and atomic number 24.

Despite resembling an unrelated shrub in leaf and flower shape, this shade-loving carrot-family plant has spread worldwide as an invasive garden escapee since being introduced as an ornamental — what is it?
Aegopodium podagraria is a species of flowering plant in the carrot family Apiaceae that grows in shady places.
These mostly semiaquatic vertebrates are tetrapods that pointedly lack an amniotic membrane, splitting into just three living orders like the frogs and toads of Anura — what are they?
Amphibian are ectothermic, anamniotic, four-limbed vertebrate animals that constitute the class Amphibia.

Once classified as bacteria and originally called archaebacteria, this domain of mostly single-celled prokaryotic organisms turns out to be the ancestral lineage from which eukaryotes evolved — which domain of life?
Archaea (ar-KEE-) is a domain of organisms.
Born in 1655, this Italian instrument maker earned lasting fame for inventing a keyboard instrument that could play both soft and loud — who was he?
Bartolomeo Cristofori (Italian; May 4, 1655 - January 27, 1731) was an Italian maker of musical instruments famous for inventing the piano.
Caused by a recessive allele in the leopard but a dominant one in the jaguar, this dark melanistic variant still secretly carries its usual rosettes — what is it called?
Black panther is the melanistic colour variant of the leopard (Panthera pardus) and the jaguar (Panthera onca).
Every one of this genus's seven woody species is toxic enough to rival deadly nightshade, and none survive in the wild anymore — only in gardens — which genus?
Brugmansia is a genus of seven species of flowering plants in the nightshade family Solanaceae.

This group of diseases directly affecting the heart muscle itself may show few symptoms early on but can progress to heart failure, irregular heartbeat, and an increased risk of sudden cardiac death — what condition is it?
Cardiomyopathy is a group of primary diseases of the heart muscle. In dilated cardiomyopathy the ventricles enlarge and weaken.

Once prized as refrigerants and aerosol propellants — Freon being the famous example — these halogenated compounds were phased out under the Montreal Protocol for gnawing holes in the ozone layer — what are they?
Chlorofluorocarbon (CFCs) and hydrochlorofluorocarbons (HCFCs) are fully or partly halogenated hydrocarbons that contain carbon (C), hydrogen (H), chlorine (Cl), and fluorine (F).

This icy small body from the outer Solar System develops a glowing atmosphere called a coma, and sometimes a tail, as it warms and releases gases when passing near the Sun — name this celestial object?
Comet is an icy, small Solar System body or interstellar object that warms and begins to release gases when passing close to the Sun, a process called outgassing.
A bright yellow polyphenol found in turmeric, a member of the ginger family, this compound is sold as an herbal supplement, cosmetic ingredient, food flavoring, and food coloring — which compound?
Curcumin is a bright yellow chemical produced by the plant species Curcuma longa.
Known from thousands of fossils pulled from the La Brea Tar Pits, this extinct species of canine roamed the Americas until about 10,000 years ago. Name the species?
Dire wolf (Aenocyon dirus) is an extinct species of canine which was native to the Americas during the Late Pleistocene and Early Holocene epochs (125,000-10,000 years ago).
Working with George de Hevesy, this Hungarian chemist theorized that diffusion speed depends on a nuclide's mass and became the world's go-to expert at preparing polonium — who was she?
Elizabeth Rona (20 March 1890 - 27 July 1981) was a Hungarian nuclear chemist, known for her work with radioactive isotopes.
Distinct from secretion, this bodily process includes exhaling carbon dioxide, sweating, and passing urine through the bladder and urethra — what's it called?
Excretion is elimination of metabolic waste, which is an essential process in all organisms.
This American political scientist argued in a controversial 1992 book that the spread of liberal democracy and free markets might be the final form of human government — who is he?
Francis Fukuyama (born October 27, 1952) is an American political scientist, political economist, and international relations scholar.

This metabolic pathway builds glucose from non-carbohydrate sources, occurring mainly in the liver in vertebrates, and serves as one of the body's two main tools for maintaining blood sugar — what process is it?
Gluconeogenesis (GNG) is a metabolic pathway that results in the biosynthesis of glucose from certain non-carbohydrate carbon substrates.

Also called the harlequin or multicoloured Asian type, this exceptionally variable insect established itself across Africa and South America after being introduced beyond its native Asia — what species?
Harmonia axyridis is a lady beetle or ladybird species that is most commonly known as the harlequin, Asian, or multicoloured Asian lady beetle.

This broad academic category studies human society, culture, and its fundamental questions — during the Renaissance, the term specifically meant the study of classical literature and language as a secular alternative to religious studies. Name the category?
Humanities are academic disciplines that study aspects of human society and culture, including certain fundamental questions asked by humans.

This pathogen has caused seasonal flu in humans and also infects birds and some mammals; strains circulate constantly in bats, pigs, horses, and dogs. It was the cause of the Spanish Flu pandemic from 1918 to 1920. What is it?
Influenza A virus is a pathogen with strains that cause seasonal flu in humans; it can also infect birds and some mammals.
Best known for his laws of planetary motion, this German astronomer has also been called the 'father of science fiction' for his novel Somnium. Who is he?
Johannes Kepler (27 December 1571 - 15 November 1630) was a German polymath who was an astronomer, mathematician, astrologer, natural philosopher and music theorist.
Named after the American endocrinologist who identified it in the 1940s, this chromosome anomaly, also called 47,XXY, typically affects phenotypic males with infertility. What condition is it?
Klinefelter syndrome (KS), also known as 47,XXY, is a chromosome anomaly.
At the time of her death, this French heiress and cosmetics-empire shareholder was the richest woman in the world, worth over $44 billion. Who is she?
Liliane Bettencourt (ne Schueller; 21 October 1922 - 21 September 2017) was a French heiress, socialite and businesswoman.
Which group of vividly colored, long-tailed New World parrots — prized in aviculture though some species face conservation concerns — belongs to the tribe Arini?
Macaw are a group of large New World parrots that are long-tailed and often colorful, in the tribe Arini.
Ranging from Patagonia to Bolivia during the Ice Age, this genus of giant ground sloths includes a type species that could weigh nearly four tonnes — which genus?

Megatherium (meg--; from Greek mga 'great' + theron 'beast') is an extinct genus of large ground sloths endemic to South America that lived from the Early Pliocene through the end of the Late Pleistocene.
This New World songbird mimics the calls of other species, insects, and frogs, and serves as the state bird of five U.S. states — which bird?
Mockingbird are a group of New World passerine bird from the family Mimidae.

It's the inherent character of the universe as a whole — the laws, elements, and phenomena of the physical world, including life itself — even though humans are often spoken of as somehow apart from it. What is it?
Nature is an inherent character or constitution, particularly of the ecosphere or the universe as a whole.
Despite counting the killer whale and pilot whale among its roughly forty species, this marine mammal family is more closely related to porpoises than to true whales — what family is it?
Oceanic dolphin are a widely distributed family of dolphins that live in the sea.
Located above, below, between, and behind the eyes, these four paired air-filled cavities take their names from the skull bones that contain them — what are they?
Paranasal sinuses are a group of four paired air-filled spaces that surround the nasal cavity.

This insect order's scientific name derives from the Ancient Greek word for 'apparition' or 'phantom' — fitting for a group whose members are famous for disguising themselves as twigs and leaves. What order is this?
Phasmatodea (also known as Phasmida or Phasmatoptera) are an order of insects whose members are variously known as stick insects, stick bugs, walkingsticks, stick animals, or bug sticks.

This large, nearly ubiquitous family of flowering plants provides the world's cereal crops, bamboo, and the plants used in lawns and pastures, ranking as the fifth-largest plant family with roughly 12,000 species — what family is this?
Poaceae (poh-(y)e), also called Gramineae (gr-(y)e), is a large and nearly ubiquitous family of monocotyledonous flowering plants commonly known as true grasses.
This Gram-negative, rod-shaped bacterium selectively blocks antibiotics from crossing its outer membrane, making it a notorious cause of hospital-acquired pneumonia — what is it?
Pseudomonas aeruginosa is a common encapsulated, Gram-negative, aerobic-facultatively anaerobic, rod-shaped bacterium that can cause disease in plants and animals, including humans.

Almost exclusively affecting girls and emerging between 6 and 18 months of age, this genetic disorder, caused mainly by mutations in the MECP2 gene, brings repetitive movements, slowed growth, and language impairment — which condition?
Rett syndrome (RTT) is a genetic disorder that typically becomes apparent after 6-18 months of age and almost exclusively in girls.
Named for the Latin word for willow tree, from which it was first derived, this plant hormone is both a precursor to aspirin and a common ingredient in anti-acne skincare — which compound?
Salicylic acid is an organic compound with the formula C7H6O3.
Setting a world record for mental calculation at London's Imperial College in 1980, this self-taught Indian prodigy also wrote books on math, puzzles, and astrology — who is she?
Shakuntala Devi (4 November 1929 - 21 April 2013) was an Indian mental calculator, astrologer, and writer, popularly known as the "Human Computer".
This family of roughly 1,450 moth species, with narrow wings and streamlined bodies built for fast, hovering flight, are so nimble they're routinely mistaken for hummingbirds — what are they called?
Sphingidae are a family of moths commonly called sphinx moths, also colloquially known as hawk moths, with many of their caterpillars known as hornworms.
These large waterfowl of the genus Cygnus are close relatives of geese and ducks, and are known for typically mating for life. What birds are they?
Swan are birds of the genus Cygnus within the family Anatidae.
Writing in 1798, this English cleric-economist warned that abundance only fuels population growth, eventually restoring poverty and hardship for the lower classes — who is he?
Thomas Robert Malthus (13/14 February 1766 - 29 December 1834) was an English economist, cleric, and scholar influential in the fields of political economy and demography.

Entering Soviet service in the 1960s, this jet was the USSR's first supersonic bomber to reach production, though it disappointed with poor range and proved notoriously hard to fly — what aircraft is it?
Tupolev Tu-22 (Air Standardization Coordinating Committee name: Blinder) was the first supersonic bomber to enter production in the Soviet Union.
Leading organic chemistry at DuPont's Experimental Station, this troubled chemist not only invented nylon but also helped lay the groundwork for neoprene. Who was he?
Wallace Carothers (April 27, 1896 - April 29, 1937) was an American chemist, inventor, and the leader of organic chemistry at DuPont, who was credited with the invention of nylon.

First identified in 1789 and not manufactured at scale until the 1920s, this corrosion-resistant, silvery-grey metal resembles hafnium and takes its name from the mineral that remains its main source — what element, symbol Zr, is it?
Zirconium is a chemical element; it has symbol Zr and atomic number 40.
Made by the adrenal glands, this hormone powers the fight-or-flight response — boosting blood flow to muscles, dilating pupils and raising blood sugar by hitting alpha and beta receptors. What is it?
Adrenaline: Hormone and medication. It appears as a white microcrystalline granule.
This Austrian psychotherapist broke from Freud's circle to found 'individual psychology,' emphasizing birth order and coining the term 'inferiority complex' — who was he?
First identified as a chemical in 1887 and later marketed as the drug Benzedrine, this CNS stimulant is prescribed today for ADHD and narcolepsy — which drug?
Designed in 1957 by a Soviet bureau and known to NATO as 'Coke,' this 50-seat twin-turboprop airliner is still license-built in China under a different name — which aircraft?
Antonov An-24: Soviet turboprop airplane. The aircraft was manufactured by the Kyiv, Irkutsk and Ulan-Ude Aviation Factories.
Also nicknamed the toddy cat or musang, this small viverrid native to South and Southeast Asia is IUCN-listed as least concern yet still poached for the illegal wildlife trade — what is it?
Asian palm civet: Species of mammal.

A North American bird of prey and sea eagle, found near large open water and old-growth forest. Its range spans most of Canada, Alaska, the contiguous U.S., and northern Mexico. This is the national bird of the United States. What is it?
Bald eagle: Bird of prey species of North America.
According to scholar John Carter, this discipline has two senses: a list of works consulted by an author, and the systematic study of books as physical objects — what's it called?
Bibliography: Organized listing of books and the systematic description of them as objects.

A four-engined American heavy bomber from the 1930s, it dropped more tonnage than any other aircraft in World War II and ranks as the third-most produced bomber in history, after the B-24 and German Ju 88—what is this legendary aircraft?

Boeing B-17 Flying Fortress: American heavy bomber aircraft. The Boeing B-17 Flying Fortress is an American four-engined heavy bomber aircraft that was developed in the mid-1930s for the United States Army Air Corps (USAAC).
Also known as undulant fever or Malta fever, this disease is usually caught by drinking unpasteurized milk from infected animals and tends to persist for life — what is it?

Roughly a third of deaths from this group of over 100 diseases trace to tobacco, alcohol, obesity, poor diet and inactivity, and its malignant tumors are defined by uncontrolled cell growth that can spread — what is it?

Cancer: Group of diseases involving cell growth. Cancer is a group of diseases involving uncontrolled cell growth typically resulting in tumors with the potential to invade or spread to other parts of the body.
An obligate carnivore with retractable claws and crepuscular hunting habits, this small domesticated mammal communicates with everything from purrs and trills to hisses — what is it?
Cat: Small domesticated carnivorous mammal. The cat (Felis catus), also called domestic cat and house cat, is a small domesticated carnivorous mammal.
Known by the common name 'greater celandine,' this perennial flowering plant belongs to the poppy family and is native to Europe and western Asia — what's its scientific name?
Chelidonium majus: Species of flowering plant in the poppy family. One of two species in the genus Chelidonium, it is native to Europe and western Asia and introduced widely in North America.
A political scientist studying voter turnout and race, this scholar rose through Harvard's deanships to become its 30th president in 2023 — only to resign months later; who is she?
Claudine Gay: American political scientist and university administrator (born 1970)

Nocturnal and marked with narrow white crossbands on a bluish-black body, this South Asian snake's potent neurotoxic venom places it among the region's 'Big Four' most dangerous species — which snake?
Common krait: Species of snake. The common krait (Bungarus caeruleus) is a highly venomous snake species belonging to the genus Bungarus in the family Elapidae.
These feather-gilled freshwater crustaceans share their taxonomic order with lobsters and turn up in everything from brooks to rice paddies — what are they?
Crayfish: Freshwater crustaceans. Crayfish are freshwater crustaceans belonging to the infraorder Astacidea, which also contains lobsters.
The first Western European combat aircraft to break Mach 2 in level flight, achieving the feat in October 1958, which French fighter jet family was this?
Dassault Mirage III: French supersonic fighter/interceptor aircraft.

Discovered in Arizona in the 1940s and first classified as a species of Megalosaurus, this theropod was reassigned to a new genus in 1970 once paleontologists noticed the twin crests on its skull — which dinosaur?
Dilophosaurus: Genus of theropod dinosaur from the Early Jurassic.

Coined by Robert Spitzer in the late 1970s to replace the notion of a "depressive personality," this condition resembles major depression but lingers for at least two years — and now goes by "persistent depressive disorder." What was its original name?
Dysthymia: Psychiatric disorder defined by chronic depression.
Caused by viruses like herpes simplex or rabies, this inflammation of the brain can bring fever, confusion, and a stiff neck — what is this condition?

Encephalitis: Inflammation of the brain. The severity can be variable with symptoms including reduction or alteration in consciousness, aphasia, headache, fever, confusion, a stiff neck, and vomiting.
This complex-analysis identity states that e raised to the power of ix equals cosine x plus i times sine x, linking exponential and trigonometric functions — what is it called?
Euler's formula: Complex exponential in terms of sine and cosine. The formula is still valid if x is a complex number, and is also called Euler's formula in this more general case.
Carnivora splits into two suborders, dog-like and cat-like — which one groups cats, hyenas, mongooses, and viverrids together?
Found at the end of the leg and typically featuring claws or nails, which weight-bearing body part enables locomotion in many vertebrates?
Foot: Anatomical structure found in vertebrates.

In 1974 in Pacific Grove, California, this computer scientist demoed the first working prototype of CP/M and invented the BIOS, then founded Digital Research to sell his software — who was this PC-revolution pioneer?
Gary Kildall: American computer scientist and microcomputer entrepreneur (1942–1994)

Making up about 15% of all brain tumors and thought to arise from cells called astrocytes, this aggressive cancer often announces itself only with vague headaches or sudden personality changes — what is it?
Glioblastoma: Aggressive type of brain cancer. Initial signs and symptoms of glioblastoma are nonspecific.
Marketed under the brand name Mucinex, this expectorant medication has been used to loosen chest congestion since at least 1933 — what is it?
Guaifenesin: Expectorant medication. It may be used in combination with other medications.

Formally described only in 1983, this helical, flagella-driven bacterium burrows through the stomach's mucous lining and is the chief culprit behind gastric ulcers and some stomach cancers. What is it?
Nicknamed 'Hobbit,' this extinct species of small archaic humans stood about 1.1 meters tall and lived on the Indonesian island of Flores until roughly 50,000 years ago — which species?
Homo floresiensis: Extinct small human species found in Flores.
Distinct from a process that adds more cells, this one is an increase in the size of individual cells, like the uterus enlarging during pregnancy — what's it called?
Hypertrophy: Increase in the size of biological cells. Hypertrophy can lead to a relative increase in the volume of a tissue or organ, and contributes to the overall growth of an organism.
Besides NASA, Roscosmos, ESA and JAXA, the fifth partner agency running the space station belongs to which country?
The Canadian Space Agency is the fifth partner. China is not a partner at all -- it built its own station, Tiangong.
A PayPal engineer who built its real-time anti-fraud system, he co-founded a famous video site and uploaded its very first clip, 'Me at the zoo,' back in April 2005. Who is he?
Jawed Karim: American entrepreneur and software engineer (born 1979)
This evergreen conifer in the cypress family has the largest geographical range of any woody plant on Earth, spanning the cool temperate Northern Hemisphere. What is it?
Juniperus communis: Species of tree in the cypress family.
Derived from the design of the Vought F-8 Crusader, this subsonic carrier-based light attack aircraft replaced the Douglas Skyhawk and saw extensive action in the Vietnam War — which aircraft?
LTV A-7 Corsair II: American attack aircraft family.
This Chinese herbalist, martial artist, and tactical advisor died in 1933 having allegedly been born in 1677 — a longevity claim gerontologists dismiss as myth. Who was he?
Li Ching-Yuen: Chinese herbalist (died 1933). Li's year of birth was alleged to be 1677, though his true age has never been determined.
This Berkeley professor gave us "fuzzy" everything — fuzzy sets, fuzzy logic, fuzzy control — proposing a whole branch of mathematics for reasoning with imprecision. Who was he?
Known by the common English name 'mallow,' this plant genus bears palmately lobed leaves and five-petaled flowers ranging from pink to white — which genus?
Originally designated the DC-9 Series 80, this five-abreast single-aisle airliner first flew in October 1979 and entered service with launch customer Swissair the following year — what jet is it?
McDonnell Douglas MD-80: Jet airliner model, series based on the DC-9.
Despite little formal schooling, this self-taught English scientist uncovered the principles behind electromagnetic induction and established the concept of the electromagnetic field — who is he?
Michael Faraday: English chemist and physicist (1791–1867)
Born in Taiwan but naturalized in Japan, this businessman invented the world's first prepackaged instant noodle brand and later created Cup Noodles — who is he?
Momofuku Ando: Taiwanese-Japanese inventor and businessman (1910–2007)
Also called flystrike, this parasitic condition occurs when fly larvae infest and feed on the tissue of a living animal — what is it?
This 17th-century Dane was a pioneer of both anatomy and geology — he doubted that fossils "grew" in the ground — before becoming a Catholic bishop and being beatified by the Church. Who was he?
Nicolas Steno: Danish scientist and Catholic bishop (1638 – 1686)
This order of predatory flying insects includes dragonflies and damselflies, whose aquatic larvae are voracious carnivores capable of overpowering small fish and tadpoles — what is it called?
Odonata: Order of insects that includes the dragonflies and damselflies. The adults are superb aerial hunters and their legs are specialised for catching prey in flight.

Powered by NADH and FADH₂ handed off from glycolysis and the citric acid cycle, this mitochondrial pathway is how nearly all aerobic organisms produce ATP — far more efficiently than fermentation. What's it called?
Oxidative phosphorylation: Metabolic pathway. Oxidative phosphorylation uses these molecules and O2 to produce ATP, which is used throughout the cell whenever energy is needed.
First domesticated in Neolithic China, this tree's fruit comes in a fuzzy form and a glossy-skinned twin called the nectarine — what fruit, a rose-family relative of the cherry and plum?
Peach: Type of fruit tree, or its fruit.
The body produces about a quart of this substance daily to trap airborne particles and bacteria — coughed up, it's also known as sputum. What is it?
Phlegm: Mucus produced by the respiratory system (excluding the nasal passages)
Commonly called frangipani, this fragrant flowering shrub native to Mexico and the Caribbean is now a beloved ornamental in Hawaii and desert climates of Arabia — what genus is it?
Plumeria: Genus of flowering plants endemic to the Americas.
Defined as supervising a team to hit all its goals within three primary constraints — scope, time, and budget — what is this discipline?
Project management: Practice of leading the work of a team to achieve goals and criteria at a specified time.

Found across Africa, Asia, and Australia, this family of nonvenomous snakes — including some of the world's largest — must coil around prey and squeeze it into cardiac arrest before swallowing it whole. What is the family?
Pythonidae: Family of snakes. The taxonomy of pythons has evolved, and they are now known to be more closely related to sunbeam snakes and the Mexican burrowing python.
Spanning turtles, crocodilians, the lizards-and-snakes of Squamata, and the lone tuatara, which group of ectothermic, amniotic animals does herpetology study?
Reptile: Class of animals. The study of the traditional reptile orders, customarily in combination with the study of modern amphibians, is called herpetology.
With over three hundred species and tens of thousands of cultivars, this thorny, often-fragrant flowering shrub blooms in shades from white to pink, red, orange, and yellow — which plant?
This colorless, odorless nerve agent can kill within minutes of inhalation and was banned by the 1993 Chemical Weapons Convention — what is it?
Sarin: Chemical compound and chemical warfare nerve agent.
A slender African cat with a tiny head and enormous ears, this golden, black-spotted hunter is the sole member of its genus and stands tall on remarkably long legs — which wild cat is it?
Known commonly as baking soda, this white crystalline compound with the formula NaHCO3 occurs naturally as the mineral nahcolite — what is its chemical name?
Sodium bicarbonate: Chemical compound. It is a salt composed of a sodium cation (Na+) and a bicarbonate anion (HCO−3).
A spherical, gram-positive bacterium that usually lives harmlessly on our skin and in our airways, this microbe can turn opportunistic and cause abscesses, sinusitis, and food poisoning — what is it?
Staphylococcus aureus: Species of Gram-positive bacterium. It is often positive for catalase and nitrate reduction and is a facultative anaerobe, meaning that it can grow without oxygen.
Among the largest flighted birds in their range, these waterfowl of genus Cygnus typically mate for life and lay three to eight eggs per clutch — what are they?
Swan: Tribe of large water birds.
In physics, temperature measures which property of a system's particles?
Temperature is an average, which is why a spark at 1000 degrees carries far less energy than a bathtub at 40 -- the bath has vastly more particles and so more total heat.
The largest cat of the genus Panthera, this Asian apex predator wears orange fur with mostly vertical black stripes and ranges from snowy Russian forests to tropical Indian jungles — what is it?
Closely related to salmon, these carnivorous freshwater fish spawn in shallow gravel beds of headwater creeks after migrating upstream — what are they called?
Trout: Freshwater fish from subfamily Salmoninae.
Used to treat epilepsy and stabilize mood in bipolar disorder, this medication carries a serious risk of birth defects if taken during pregnancy — what is it?
Valproate: Medication used for epilepsy, bipolar disorder and migraine. Common side effects of valproate include nausea, vomiting, somnolence, and dry mouth.
Also known as ash pumpkin or winter melon, this South and Southeast Asian plant is grown for its very large fruit, eaten as a vegetable once mature — which plant?
Wax gourd: Species of vine and edible fruit.
This Japanese media artist and academic directs a research centre for 'Digital Nature' and holds visiting professorships at multiple Japanese art universities — who is he?
Yoichi Ochiai: Japanese academic, artist, and entrepreneur. Yoichi Ochiai (落合 陽一, Yoichi Ochiai; born 16 September 1987) is a Japanese media artist, entrepreneur, and academic.
What is the chemical symbol for tin?
The symbol for tin is Sn. Tin is a chemical element; it has the symbol Sn and atomic number 50.
What is the chemical symbol for copernicium?
The symbol for copernicium is Cn. Copernicium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Cn and atomic number 112.

Adam DeVine is a comedian. Adam DeVine (born November 7, 1983) is an American comedian, actor, producer and screenwriter.
In what year was Cole Sprouse born?
Cole Sprouse: Cole Mitchell Sprouse (born August 4, 1992) is an American actor.
In what year was Taron Egerton born?
Taron Egerton (EJ-ər-tən; born 10 November 1989) is a Welsh actor.
In what year was Anna Nicole Smith born?
Anna Nicole Smith: Smith started her modeling career as a Playboy magazine centerfold in May 1992 and won the title of 1993 Playmate of the Year.
In what year was Dennis Quaid born?
Dennis Quaid: Dennis William Quaid (born April 9, 1954) is an American actor.
In what year was Lily Collins born?
Lily Collins: Lily Jane Collins (born 18 March 1989) is an English and American actress.

Kevin Spacey Fowler (born July 26, 1959) is an American actor.
In what year was Peter Dinklage born?
Peter Dinklage: Peter Hayden Dinklage (born June 11, 1969) is an American actor.
In what year was Ray Stevenson born?
Ray Stevenson: George Raymond Stevenson (25 May 1964 – 21 May 2023) was a British actor, best known for his film and television work.
In what year was Lindsay Lohan born?
Lindsay Lohan: Lindsay Dee Lohan ( LOH-ən; born July 2, 1986) is an American actress, singer, and songwriter.
In what year was Ridley Scott born?
Ridley Scott: Sir Ridley Scott (born 30 November 1937) is an English filmmaker.
In what year was Bill Skarsgård born?
Bill Skarsgård: Bill Istvan Günther Skarsgård (Swedish: [ˈbɪlː ˈskɑ̌ːʂɡoːɖ]; born 9 August 1990) is a Swedish actor, model, producer, and director.
In what year did Natasha Richardson die?
Natasha Richardson: Natasha Jane Richardson (11 May 1963 – 18 March 2009) was an English actress.
In what year was Belfast first released?
